explanation: Younger son of Isaac and Rebekah, brother to Esau, who becomes one of the patriarchs in the Hebrew tradition.
Jacob's older twin brother, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and father of the Edomites.
The event where Jacob and Esau are reunited after many years of strife and conflict.
The process by which two parties resolve their conflicts and restore a good relationship; here it refers to the reconciliation between Jacob and Esau.
Objects or actions given to express gratitude, friendship, or love; in this case, Jacob gives gifts to Esau as part of the reconciliation process.
A place mentioned in Genesis 33, where Jacob builds a house and makes shelters for his livestock after meeting Esau.
An ancient city in Canaan (present-day Israel) where Jacob settles after meeting Esau and buys land from the local inhabitants.
